qs.q: In MS Word, a user wants to ensure that a long table does not split across pages. Which feature should be adjusted?
o: Keep with next paragraph option in paragraph formatting settings
Allow row to break across pages option in table properties
Repeat header rows option in table layout configuration options
Fit to window option in layout page setup formatting settings
Lock anchor option in floating object position configuration settings
qs.e: Unchecking 'Allow row to break across pages' prevents individual table rows from splitting between sheets.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Word wants to create a table of contents that updates automatically as the document changes. What is required?
o: Utilizing footnote citations to link document section headings to body text
Manually entering page numbers for each individual structural section heading
Inserting manual page breaks immediately prior to major document chapter sections
Applying built-in heading styles to structural section titles in the document
Formatting the entire document content using a single continuous column layout
qs.e: Automatic tables of contents rely on built-in heading styles to identify and list document sections.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Word wants to ensure that a specific paragraph stays on the same page as the next one. Which setting should be used?
o: Use “keep with next” to keep this paragraph with the following one.
Enable “keep lines together” to avoid line breaks inside a paragraph.
Apply “page break before” to start the paragraph on a new page.
Turn on “widow control” to prevent a single line at the top of a page.
Turn on “orphan control” to prevent a single line at the bottom of a page.
qs.e: Keep with next ensures the current paragraph remains on the same page as the following paragraph.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Word wants to insert a page number that starts at 1 on the first page of a chapter. What is required?
o: Choose Insert > Page Number to add automatic numbering.
Manually type the page number directly into the header.
Insert a section break and set a different first‑page numbering.
Adjust page‑number formatting through the Layout tab options.
Link to the previous section’s header to continue numbering.
qs.e: Section breaks allow independent formatting of page numbering for different parts of the document.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A student needs to cite a source in a paper. Which feature in MS Word helps manage references?
o: The table‑of‑contents tool for listing document chapters.
The footnote tool for manually entering inline references.
The endnote tool for placing citations at the document’s end.
The cross‑reference tool for linking internal document elements.
The bibliography tool for automatically formatting citations.
qs.e: The bibliography tool automates citation formatting and reference list generation.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A user in MS Word wants to create a document with a cover page that is formatted differently. What is required?
o: Manual formatting rules applied exclusively to the first page
A standard page break inserted right before main content
A section break combined with a different first page setting
A header and footer feature configured for the initial page
A specific paragraph style applied directly to opening text
qs.e: Section breaks allow the first page to have distinct formatting, such as a cover page.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: ICT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
